long_biography.plain_text:
Physical chemist Crawford Fairbanks Failey studied how electrolytes changed the behaviour of dissolved compounds, bringing thermodynamic methods into biological research. His papers examined weak acids, amino acids and vapour-liquid equilibria, while his university teaching connected fundamental chemistry with medical-school laboratories.

A large inheritance arrived while Failey was a young university instructor. He chose to continue teaching and studying, then spent the following decades in research and higher education. The estate came from his grandfather, Crawford Fairbanks, a Terre Haute businessman whose interests grew from distilling and brewing into paper, property and other industrial ventures. Failey remained in academic science and belonged to the American Chemical Society until his death.

The dossier therefore resolves the person with very high confidence, proposes Dead and treats the vessel link strictly as historical identity evidence.

Feadship heritage material describes Failey as a professor of medicine, but Columbia and American Chemical Society records more precisely identify him as a physical chemist, biological-chemistry teacher and University of Chicago chemistry professor. The biographies and known-for proposal use the university and scientific-society formulation rather than presenting him as a practising physician.

Phillips Academy's contemporary yearbook gives the exact birth date and place, while the American Chemical Society supplies the exact death date and age. The grandfather's estate was diversified across distilling, brewing, paper, property, hotels, utilities and other investments. Food & Beverage is selected because specialist historical work identifies distilling as the original driving source and official histories document the substantial brewery. The classification does not imply that every inherited asset belonged to that sector.

Food & Beverage is therefore the contract's origin-sector fallback rather than a claim of personal brewery management or a current holding. Confidence is reduced to medium accordingly.
